books.title: Why Your Mortgage Moves
books.blurb: One bond yield quietly sets your home loan.
gist: The Fed sets a one-night rate between banks; a 30-year mortgage is priced off the 10-year Treasury yield plus a spread.
The Fed's rate is down 1.5 points from its peak, yet the 10-year rose to about 5.2% and mortgages to about 7.4%.
On a $300,000 loan that is about $220 a month more than a year ago.

books.blurb: Why borrowing to pay interest feeds itself.
gist: The US owes about $40 trillion and now pays over $1 trillion a year in interest, much of it with new borrowing.
Every new IOU travels through money plumbing: reserves, repo and money funds. Tight pipes make borrowing pricier.
Leveraged bets on Treasuries work until margin calls hit, and new money reaches asset owners before wage earners.

books.title: Dollar, Gold & the Yen
books.blurb: Why the dollar can be strong and still buy less.
gist: The dollar can hold steady against other currencies while buying less at the store: two different yardsticks.
Japan is the canary: huge debt, a weak yen near ¥164, and a joint US–Japan rescue in late July.
Japan's 10-year yield is the highest in about 30 years, which could mean less Japanese money lent to the US.
